A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The existing experiments and supplementary sections can be matched reliably; v2 adds Sections S5–S6.

before.justification: v1 reports original MAFW/DFEW experiments on frame shuffling, sampling density, balanced fine-tuning, visual prompting, and MSCE, plus lexical-frequency correlation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds a reported TCoT comparison and quantitative analyses of confusion asymmetry and balanced fine-tuning.

M1.justification: Balanced fine-tuning and the two-stage MSCE procedure remain unchanged, including four intermediate frames per gap and interleaved keyframe/text classification. Revised notation and the redrawn diagram do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use MAFW and DFEW for dynamic emotion recognition and English/Chinese Google Books Ngram frequencies for the bias analysis. The added comparisons and analyses use retained coverage.

E2.justification: Section 4.2 adds an evaluated TCoT comparator under a reported matched Qwen2.5-VL setup; v1 only discussed and cited TCoT. Other comparator sets remain unchanged. The newly cited specialist facial-expression methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section S5 introduces a directional-asymmetry metric and selected class-pair controls. Existing settings remain unchanged, including the 495/700-video balanced test sets, FPS sweep, approximately 1,500 fine-tuning videos, and MSCE intermediate-frame count.

E4.justification: New Sections S5–S6 quantify directional confusion and examine per-class benefits and failures of balanced fine-tuning. These extend analyses already presented through confusion matrices in v1. Existing shuffling, FPS, and visual-prompting analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The Pearson correlations, two-tailed significance testing, and p-values in Table 1 are unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or comparable uncertainty estimates for classification performance.

E6.justification: Existing Tables 1–3 and S1–S3 retain their values. v2 newly reports TCoT F1 of 0.241 on MAFW and 0.450 on DFEW, asymmetry scores, and fine-tuning summaries including macro-F1 of 0.245 zero-shot versus 0.315 after balanced fine-tuning. These are added results, not improvements between versions; Table S4 redisplays the existing Figure 3 confusion counts.

T1.justification: Section S5 adds the formal definition Δ(r,c) = f(r→c) − f(c→r), its antisymmetry property, and its interpretation for directional confusion. v1 discussed asymmetry qualitatively without this definition. Existing mathematics is otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The central long-tail-bias and temporal-bottleneck claims remain. v2 explicitly positions MSCE as a secondary diagnostic contribution and strengthens the conclusion from fundamental changes that 'may' be required to shifts that 'will' be required.

C2.justification: v2 softens proxy validation to suggestive support and adds explanations concerning English/Chinese lexical frequencies. Section S6 newly qualifies rebalancing as redistributing rather than eliminating bias, with Helplessness over-predicted and Disappointment still difficult. Gemini results are also clarified as bias measurement rather than mitigation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link and explicitly identifies MAFW in Figure 4's caption. The 7–8B model-size range repeated in the main text was already disclosed in v1 Section S2, alongside the unchanged A100 hardware information.

R1.justification: v2 adds a focused discussion of DK-CLIP, PE-CLIP, Fine-CLIPER, AU-DFER, ExpLLM, and FaVChat, positioning specialist successes as complementary to its diagnosis. It also sharpens distinctions from previously cited long-tail and SpookyBench research. Publication metadata updates concern retained works.

P1.justification: There are localized paragraph rewrites, terminology and punctuation edits, clearer contribution framing, and two new supplementary subsections. The main section sequence and most explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 5 is redrawn using video frames, timestamps, stage labels, and an explicit prediction example. v2 adds Tables S4–S6, clarifies Figure 4's caption, and relocates retained displays through page reflow. Other figures and existing table structures remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 makes previously visual confusion and fine-tuning arguments more inspectable through Sections S5–S6, adds a direct TCoT comparison, and explains MSCE more clearly in Figure 5. Its discussion also acknowledges residual and redistributed bias. These limited gains outweigh a new reporting inconsistency: S6 says 8 of 11 classes improve, whereas Table S6 shows 10. The stronger concluding necessity claim is not accompanied by evidence resolving the acknowledged causal limitations.
